parent_trial: ImPuls trial: Wolf, S., Seiffer, B., Zeibig, J.-M., Frei, A. K., Studnitz, T., Welkerling, J., ... Ehring, T. (2024). A transdiagnostic group exercise intervention for mental health outpatients in Germany (ImPuls): Results of a pragmatic, multisite, block-randomised, phase 3 controlled trial. The Lancet Psychiatry, 11(6), 417-430. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(24)00069-5. Trial registration: German Clinical Trial Register, DRKS00024152 (registered 05/02/2021).
primary_outcome_of_this_paper: Not a group-comparison primary outcome. This paper is a mediation (secondary/mechanisms) analysis of the ImPuls RCT. It reuses the parent trial's primary outcome, the Global Severity Index (GSI, derived from the German BSI-18), at 6 and 12 months as the dependent variable in structural equation (path) mediation models, but the paper's own analytic target is the indirect (mediated) effect of treatment on GSI change via three mediators: perceived stress, repetitive negative thinking, and sleep quality. Abstract: 'As a secondary analysis of an RCT, intention-to-treat analyses were performed using structural equation modeling to test whether changes in stress perception, repetitive negative thinking, and sleep quality mediate treatment effects on changes in global symptom severity...'. Methods (Outcomes/Primary outcome paragraph): 'Global symptom severity at 6 months assessed with the Global Severity Index (GSI) derived from the German version of the Brief Symptom Inventory-18 (Franke, 2017), served as the primary outcome and endpoint of the efficacy study (Wolf et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2024). Therefore, the GSI at both 6 months post intervention and 12 months follow-up were utilized as primary outcome in the mediation analyses conducted in the present study.' Introduction: 'The current study represents a secondary analysis of the ImPuls trial, focusing on three key processes common to these conditions: stress perception, repetitive negative thinking, and sleep quality.' and 'This report is a secondary analysis of the ImPuls trial (Wolf et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2024)...'.
reason: The paper explicitly identifies itself as a secondary/mediation analysis of the already-published ImPuls trial (Wolf et al. 2024, The Lancet Psychiatry), not a primary trial report. It has no primary outcome or primary group-contrast estimate of its own; it borrows the parent trial's primary outcome (GSI) as the dependent variable in a mediation/SEM framework and reports indirect effects (beta coefficients for mediated paths), not a treatment-vs-control mean difference on a primary outcome. Confirmed individual-participant data are deposited in the study's own deposit folder (e.g. Impuls_PAHCOchanges_V2_open.csv has an 'id', 'rand_group' arm indicator (0/1), 'timepoint' (0/1/2), and 'BSI18_sum', i.e. the BSI-18-derived GSI outcome), so IPD with arm and the (parent trial's) primary outcome exist and could in principle be used to reanalyse the ImPuls primary comparison directly -- but that primary comparison belongs to the parent Lancet Psychiatry paper, not to this PMC12885332 paper. Given the project's registry only lists PMC12885332 (not the parent Lancet Psychiatry paper) and no registry.csv row exists for this study_id, and the paper itself is a mediation/mechanisms analysis rather than a primary efficacy report, it should be excluded from the primary-analysis extraction batch. If the multiverse-reanalysis project wants to include the ImPuls trial's own primary GSI comparison, the correct source paper is Wolf et al. 2024 (Lancet Psychiatry, DOI 10.1016/S2215-0366(24)00069-5), not this secondary analysis; the IPD found here could still serve that purpose since it contains id/arm/timepoint/GSI, but a new study_id and registry.csv row keyed to the parent trial paper would be needed.
